newsitem.title: UK: ICCO sees long-term cocoa stock ratio at 34 pct.
newsitem.headline: ICCO sees long-term cocoa stock ratio at 34 pct.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) has forecast the long-term world cocoa stocks-to-grindings (consumption) ratio at 34 percent, delegates to the ICCO meeting said.

The producer-consumer group had in June put the ratio -- a barometer of prices -- at 47.5 percent or five-and-a-half months of world consumption of 2.68 million tonnes by the end of the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) crop year.
Delegates to the week-long ICCO council meeting which opened in London on Monday said no central target for the ratio, the basis of the grouping's production plan, had been fixed yet.

Historically, cocoa prices have taken an upturn each time the ratio fell below the 30 percent threshold. But conference sources said there were reservations at the meeting about reliable data on stocks, held privately in most consumer countries.
"There are certain amount of doubts on stock figures," a source told Reuters.

The London-based ICCO administers the five-year cocoa agreement, which tries to implement voluntary production cuts by 75,000 tonnes a year or 375,000 tonnes over five years from 1994 needed to help balance world supply and demand.
But the so-called production management plan has been beset by overproduction by some key members.
The ICCO moved last June to set a central output target by a four percent corridor on both sides to allow for weather factors. The previous single-point target has so far been missed.
But a decision on new output goals was deferred to this week's meeting.
Delegates said several top producers such as Ivory Coast were expected to contest the ICCO secretariat's draft proposals outlining output targets and the possible output cuts to meet the targets.
